purpose: Same-commit ordinary native JavaScript caller supplement; frozen v1 unchanged

facts.fact: The ordinary JavaScriptExecuteRequest executes the authored native ClassicScript Program in the document main world and, when a result is requested, creates the platform WebV8ValueConverter, sets DateAllowed=true and RegExpAllowed=true, then calls GetJavaScriptExecutionResult.

GetJavaScriptExecutionResult calls converter.FromV8Value exactly once for a nonempty completion. If conversion yields nullptr, the ordinary return is base::Value() (null), which the shown Android callback serializes to raw null text.

This ordinary caller does not set FunctionAllowed, StripNullFromObjects, ConvertNegativeZeroToInt or Strategy. Under the bound converter constructor these remain false/false/false/null; Date and RegExp must not be treated as constructor defaults.

With the explicitly requested DateAllowed=true, the bound converter turns Date into ValueOf()/1000.0 (seconds as a double), not JSON.stringify ISO text. RegExpAllowed=true returns its string representation, not an empty object. Both belong in WK native information-preservation characterization.
Plain ordinary execution does not use the ForTests resolve_promises setting or an async-function wrapper. No Promise-resolution contract is inferred from the neighboring test-only method.

remainingBindingLimits: The concrete Platform::CreateWebV8ValueConverter factory adapter is outside the one-source supplement; the exact caller setters are proven and converter implementation behavior is separately bound. This is source-contract evidence, not runtime Android verification.
The Chromium commit is fixed, but no particular installed Android WebView release or source app device result is claimed.
characterizationImpact: Test Date/RegExp alongside the original ten information-loss groups. Distinguish ordinary caller flags from defaults in source-derived expectations; never mark existing captured JSON.stringify characterization as Android-compatible.
